evidence.evidence_text: A line of work on Transformer-based language models such as BERT has attempted to use syntactic inductive bias to enhance the pretraining process, on the theory that building syntactic structure into the training process should reduce the amount of data needed for training.
In this work, we investigate whether these methods can compensate for data sparseness in low-resource languages, hypothesizing that they ought to be more effective for low-resource languages.
We experiment with five low-resource languages: Uyghur, Wolof, Maltese, Coptic, and Ancient Greek.
